body:
Raised from **G4** in [`plans/gsc-page-optimization-2026-11.md`](https://github.com/fardintolo123/elite-touch-revonations/blob/main/plans/gsc-page-optimization-2026-11.md#g4--clarify-the-diy-decision-and-homeowner-preparation-path).

## Problem and first-party evidence
The current live DIY guide has three broad decision sections and no FAQ. It does not route readers to the existing first-time sequence or the checklist. The literal “1)” opening is an editorial defect. Do not make a second general workflow article when the first-time guide already owns that explanation.

| Query on this URL | Impressions | Position |
|---|---:|---:|
| how to renovate a bathroom | 189 | 22.2 |
| diy bathroom renovation | 121 | 19.8 |
| renovating a bathroom | 112 | 24.0 |
| can you renovate a bathroom yourself | 58 | 25.4 |

Current NSW waterproofing guidance states a contractor-licence threshold of more than $5,000 in labour/materials including GST. Re-check official current guidance before writing a blanket licensing claim: [NSW Government waterproofing work](https://www.nsw.gov.au/business-and-economy/licences-and-credentials/building-and-trade-licences-and-registrations/waterproofing-work). The existing article's blanket statement must not be expanded uncritically.

## Scope
`lib/blog.ts` — `diy-or-professional-bathroom-renovation`, selected contextual-link paragraphs in `first-time-bathroom-renovation-sydney` and/or `bathroom-renovation-budget-planning`

## Required change
1. Explain the homeowner's decision: scope, who coordinates the trades, what must be checked before doing any work, disruption and risks of rework. Remove the stray numbered prefix and give a clear first answer.
2. Verify any statements about regulated plumbing/electrical/waterproofing work and owner-builder responsibilities against current official NSW sources. Distinguish ETR's own licensed-renovation process from universal legal requirements; link sources. Avoid legal conclusions beyond what those sources establish.
3. Use natural DIY metadata/H1 and useful question headings/FAQs. A possible concise meta title is “DIY Bathroom Renovation in NSW”; verify the full rendered title. No savings, costs, completion-time guarantees or step-by-step regulated-work instructions.
4. Link the complete renovation sequence to `/blog/first-time-bathroom-renovation-sydney/`, practical checks to the existing checklist and time expectations to the duration owner.
5. Where it adds real help, link back from the existing first-time or budget article's own DIY/coordination discussion. Do not rewrite those donor articles or create a duplicate how-to page.

## Acceptance criteria
- The DIY-versus-managed decision is immediately clear and there is a useful preparation path.
- Every load-bearing licensing statement has a current official source, or is removed/qualified; ETR practice is not presented as universal law.
- Existing first-time/checklist/timeline owners receive relevant contextual links and donor links work.
- FAQ answers are useful, plain text and schema-consistent; no unsafe procedural tutorial or invented outcome is added.

## Evidence and constraints
Finalized GSC **web** query+page data, **2026-08-05–2026-11-02**, property `sc-domain:elitetouchrenovations.au`. Figures below are query/page impressions and rounded average positions, not search volumes. The >=10-impression screen only generated candidates; these changes have additional source and live-page evidence. No country/device/recurrence/trend claim is supported. Full evidence: `session-history/evidence/2026-11-05-gsc-optimization/` (raw response, live snapshot, screening CSV and independent review).

Read `CLAUDE.md`, `docs/SEO_CONTENT_GUIDE.md`, `docs/CONTENT_QUALITY_CHECKLIST.md`, `docs/SEO_AEO_GEO_CHECKLIST.md`, `DESIGN.md` and relevant decisions. Use current business facts only. No new URL, invented number/project/review, dependency, client boundary, artificial freshness or service claim. FAQ answers remain plain text and must match visible FAQ JSON-LD. Image alt/captions describe the actual existing photo; retain descriptive filenames unless inspection establishes a genuine defect. Do not insert query variants into every field. Record KEEP when metadata/headings/media already meet intent.

## Verification and publication
- Save a before/after query-to-section map and reasons for KEEP/reject/routing decisions. Verify actual served HTML, final canonical, rendered title/description (including brand template), one H1, content/FAQ parity and working contextual links.
- Build: `npm run build --ignore-scripts`; `npm run typecheck`; `npm run check:design`; `npm run check:readability` with its inventory reconciled against published built routes. Run builds in isolation; preserve concurrent work.
- Browser checks at 390×844 and 1440×900; content additions need budget-aware before/after measurement, and visual changes need independent critique with no P0/P1.
- Commit task-owned changes only. The owner has authorized pushing this verified SEO work to live. Inspect all commits included in a push; never bundle unrelated unverified edits. Re-fetch production and verify changed copy/links before reporting shipped.
- Record deployment date and exact query/page cohorts. Compare finalized equal-length windows after recrawl, with enquiries/call events where available. Do not claim rank or enquiry gains at deployment time.

## Parallelization
- Can run in parallel: **NO**.
- Depends on: **#94**.
- Files owned:
- `lib/blog.ts` (only the named post objects; limit donor edits to contextual links)
- Must not modify:
  - `app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx`, `app/blog/page.tsx`, `app/blog/blog.module.css` (existing template work).
  - `lib/businessInfo.ts`, `lib/hubContent.ts`, `lib/projects.ts`, `lib/suburbContent.ts`, `service-areas.json`, `next.config.ts`.
  - `scripts/check-readability.mjs`, `app/globals.css`, `CLAUDE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `PROJECT_CONTEXT.md` and any unlisted post object.
- Acceptance criteria: the concrete checklist above, plus the shared evidence/publication gate.
- Verification: the narrow served-HTML/link/FAQ checks above, then the required build, readability and responsive checks.
- Reason: all five deliverables edit the same physical `lib/blog.ts` file; execute G1 → G2 → G3 → G4 → G5. #91 itself waits for current concurrent description edits to be committed. Never run alongside active #88–#90 edits; verify their state rather than redoing completed work.
title: [GSC] Improve the DIY bathroom decision guide with verified NSW scope and useful next steps
